raw_response:
My land is about 12 mu, same fields my family has worked for decades. Here in Quzhou, everyone grows wheat and corn — one after the other on the same ground. That's just how it is. Winter wheat goes in after the fall holiday in October, comes out in June. Then I turn around and plant corn right away, harvest in September before it gets cold. Two harvests, same land. That's how you make ends meet.

I'll buy the Jimai wheat variety the village seed shop sells — it's what my neighbor used last year and he did well. For corn I always get a hybrid, the Xianyu or Pioneer kind. Traditional seeds aren't worth the gamble anymore.

Fertilizer — I put down diammonium phosphate and potash before I plow in the wheat, then come back with urea when the wheat starts jointing in spring. For corn I fertilize at planting and again when it's knee-high. My son says we put down too much nitrogen but I've seen what happens when you scrimp — a thin stand or a dry spell wipes you out. I'm not going to risk that.

I have an electric pump on the well. Wheat needs water four times at least — when it goes in, before it freezes, at jointing, and when the grain fills. Corn I water twice, more if the summer's dry. The last few years have been dry, so I'll be watching it.

Pesticides: herbicide in autumn and spring for wheat, fungicide and aphid spray around heading. For corn, herbicide early and one spray for corn borer. That's it.
